questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Doubling a pitch standard up two octaves
questions.learningObjective: Read a table of pitch doublings

stimulus.body: A table lists pitch doublings: up one octave is twelve semitones; up two octaves is twenty-four.

questions.stem: In the clinician's note, the table lists doublings; how many semitones is up two octaves?
questions.explanation: Up two octaves is twenty-four semitones. The distractors under- or over-count.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Telling a monophonic texture from a polyphonic one
questions.stem: In the clinician's note, how do you tell monophonic from polyphonic texture?

answer.exemplar: Count the independent melodic lines: one line means monophonic; two or more independent lines mean polyphonic.

questions.explanation: Count independent lines. The written answer should mention one versus many.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Telling a madrigal from the other sacred and secular forms
questions.stem: In the clinician's note, summarise what distinguishes a madrigal.

answer.exemplar: A madrigal is a secular polyphonic vocal work that uses text painting to express the meaning of vernacular poetry.

questions.explanation: Secular polyphonic vocal work with text painting. The written answer should mention all three traits.
